title: Boot Entry Point
description: Start at the Multiboot-compliant assembly loader that sets up a 2MB kernel stack, calls global constructors, and jumps to kernelMain with multiboot info.

title: Kernel Initialization
description: The main kernel entry point where all subsystems are initialized in sequence: GDT, MemoryManager, InterruptManager, PCI bus, drivers, FAT filesystem, GUI desktop, and the full networking stack. See the initialization order in kernelMain.

title: Hardware Platform: GDT, Ports, Interrupts, PCI
description: The x86 hardware abstraction layer: GlobalDescriptorTable for segmentation, I/O port abstractions (8/16/32 bit), PIC-based interrupt handling with IDT setup, interrupt stubs in assembly, and PCI bus enumeration with automatic driver discovery.

title: Memory Management and Multitasking
description: The kernel heap allocator using a free-list-based MemoryManager (with global operator new/delete overrides), and the cooperative multitasking system with round-robin scheduling and interrupt-based syscall dispatch.

title: Device Drivers
description: The driver framework and hardware drivers: Driver base class with lifecycle, PS/2 keyboard with scancode-to-ASCII mapping, PS/2 mouse with relative motion tracking, VGA graphics (320x200x256), ATA PATA storage driver, and the AMD Am79C973 Ethernet NIC driver with DMA descriptor rings.

title: FAT Filesystem
description: Full FAT12/16/32 filesystem implementation adapted from the Arduino SdFat library. Includes MBR partition table parsing, BIOS Parameter Block reading, FAT cluster chain management, directory traversal, and file read/write operations via SdFile/SdVolume classes.

title: GUI: Desktop, Widgets, Windows
description: The graphical user interface layer with a composite widget hierarchy: Widget base class with positioning and focus, CompositeWidget with child management and event dispatch, draggable Window, and Desktop with mouse cursor rendering. Uses VGA as the GraphicsContext.

title: Network Stack: Ethernet to TCP
description: A full network stack built on the AMD NIC driver: EtherFrameProvider dispatches by etherType, ARP resolves IP-to-MAC, IPv4 provides subnet-based routing, ICMP handles ping, and UDP/TCP provide transport-layer socket abstractions with a full TCP state machine.
